content.comment_body: A [product_name] [version_no] module configured as a slave does not restart automatically after a power cycle. Each time, manual intervention is needed to start the slave; otherwise, the master and slave won’t communicate. If the slave is started manually, everything works fine, but after another power cycle, the issue returns. Factory reset did not resolve this. Is this a hardware fault, or is it expected behavior in the new [version_no] release? Any suggestions?

This seems to be a software bug in the [product_name] [version_no]. I've also encountered it, as have other users. Discussions in the German-speaking section of the forum confirm that the slave modules do not automatically return to RUN mode. So far, [company_name] has not provided an official response. It appears we’ll need to wait for an upcoming firmware or software update.

Thanks for clarifying that I’m not alone with this issue. After reading your post, it seems the latest firmware hasn't fixed the slave problem, or perhaps it resolved other issues? That part is not completely clear to me. I’ll try updating the device and see how it performs, but this setup isn’t usable as-is.
No, in the German forum I explained that the firmware update only fixes the issue with Q3 output, but the slave mode bug remains.

I saw your reply later, sorry for missing it. As expected, the update didn’t resolve the issue here either. I contacted [company_name] sales to ask about the problem, but they didn’t have a solution and suggested submitting a support request. Now, I’m waiting for their feedback.
[company_name] is aware of the bug affecting slave modules and is working on a fix, but no timeline has been provided. We'll have to be patient.

Hello, try this: set the [product_name] [version_no] slave module into RUN mode and then perform a power cycle. My own [product_name] [version_no] returns to RUN mode automatically if it was set that way before power cycling. Hopefully this helps.
This is the latest info from the support team.

Hello, I have several [product_name] [version_no] 12/24V Rce versions on my test bench and none of them restart automatically after power cycling. Which model or version are you using? Kind regards, [user_name]
Still waiting for a solution... Acquiring new [product_name] units is very difficult right now as only pre-orders are possible, and nothing is available in stock.
Has anyone found a solution to this problem yet?
No solution has been found so far. [company_name] has not yet released a firmware update to address this problem.

Hello, possible workaround: 1) Avoid disconnecting the power supply of the [product_name] slave module. 2) If using master/slave mode is problematic, try configuring both modules as masters if they are [product_name] [version_no] modules. Hope this helps.

It’s not always possible to prevent power interruptions, as outages can occur unexpectedly. If all devices are from the [version_no] series, does that mean you should simply avoid using slave mode due to a firmware issue from [company_name]? It’s disappointing that suggested solutions seem to focus on workarounds instead of actual troubleshooting.

The issue with '[product_name] [version_no] slave not restarting after power loss' was resolved after updating the firmware to [version_no]. I performed the upgrade and tested the module, and the error is gone. The update for both software and firmware can be downloaded—search for [document].

You're right, the automatic restart problem for slave modules after power cycle is now fixed—after nearly six months. Curiously, I didn’t receive a notification about your last message; otherwise I would have found out two days earlier.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering a persistent bug with [product_name] [version_no] modules used as slaves: after a power cycle, the slave does not automatically restart and requires manual intervention to enter RUN mode. The problem occurs across different units and firmware versions, and [company_name] support has acknowledged it but hasn't offered a solution for some time. Users are also experiencing difficulties in acquiring new modules due to stock issues. The problem was eventually resolved after a firmware update.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that slave [product_name] modules should automatically return to RUN mode after a power cycle, just like master modules, and that future updates will ensure stable, reliable operation without requiring manual resets.
